experienceDirection: Default to a visually led, interaction-first experience with responsive motion, spatial depth, direct manipulation, ambient state, and memorable moments worth sharing; keep explanatory text concise and integrated into the experience, while allowing richer copy when the requested format—such as a landing page, CMS, publication, or narrative archive—depends on it, and leave technology and dependency choices to the lead.
completionMandate: Every prepared actual prompt must reject shortcuts and cookie-cutter approximations while demanding complete subject-specific depth. For replicas, clones, and emulators, require faithful recreation of the original's look, feel, behavior, states, transitions, edge cases, and smallest meaningful interactions rather than a recognizable shell. For original experiences, require equivalent depth across primary and secondary interactions, motion, feedback, atmosphere, responsive states, and meaningful details. Express these requirements naturally for the requested subject instead of pasting this root value as generic boilerplate. Keep skill policy, token and delegation policy, technical schemas, tool commands, and workflow instructions in the separate operational envelope, and never prescribe a technology, library, framework, or workflow unless the user did.
